title: Soccer Calibration Pack
headline_insight: On this international-soccer corpus the market is sharper than the model: model Brier is 0.332522 versus market 0.195157 over 4,265 rows, and the gap is widest exactly where the two disagree most.
what_it_means: When model and market diverge by 0.10 or more (n=2291), the model is the closer forecast only 10.48% of the time. Late-game calibration also drifts, with expected calibration error climbing to 0.4824 in the 75-91 minute bucket. This is a published null, not a win. Segmentation cut the corpus from 9,003 rows to 4,265 and dropped the draw share from about 26% to 14% of ticks; a draw is mechanically cheap to score against a two-way probability, so both sides post a higher Brier here than they did in revision 1.
how_to_read: The Murphy decomposition splits Brier into reliability and resolution; the disagreement buckets show who is closer when model and market pull apart; the minute buckets show calibration error over the clock.
why_it_matters: It is honest market-efficiency evidence, the model does not beat the market here, reported as-is rather than hidden.
caveat: The soccer_intl corpus is only 4,265 rows across 27 games, far smaller than MLB or NBA, so confidence intervals are wide and single-fold reads are not durable.
